## Claims
- [proved] Conditional on task 85’s interval presentation and complete \(h_1\)-row hypothesis, for \(0\le k\le b=\min(i,j)\),
  \[
  M_{d+k}/L_k\cong\mathbb Z,\qquad [C_x]=(-1)^x[C_0]\quad(0\le x\le k),
  \]
  where \(C_x=P_{x,k-x}\). The isomorphism sends \([C_0]\) to \(1\).
- [proved] Put
  \[
  X_k=P_{k,0}=s_{((i+1)^k,i^{j-k})},\qquad
  Y_k=P_{0,k}=s_{(i^j,k)}.
  \]
  Then degreewise
  \[
  [X_k]=(-1)^k[Y_k],\qquad [Y_k]=(-1)^k[X_k].
  \]
  Thus the change-of-basis matrix from the horizontal endpoint basis \(([X_k])\) to the vertical endpoint basis \(([Y_k])\) is the \(1\times1\) matrix \(\bigl((-1)^k\bigr)\), for every \(0\le k\le b\).
- [proved] The requested truncated conditional target is established; no globalization claim is made.

## Strategy
For \(k\ge1\), task 85 gives
\[
M_{d+k}=\bigoplus_{x=0}^k\mathbb ZC_x,\qquad
L_k=\sum_{x=0}^{k-1}\mathbb Z(C_x+C_{x+1}).
\]
Hence \(C_{x+1}=-C_x\) in the quotient, giving \([C_x]=(-1)^x[C_0]\). The homomorphism
\[
C_x\longmapsto (-1)^x\in\mathbb Z
\]
annihilates \(L_k\) and sends \(C_0\) to \(1\), proving that \([C_0]\) has infinite order and that the quotient is \(\mathbb Z\). For \(k=0\), \(L_0=0\) and \(M_d=\mathbb ZC_0\).

## Gaps
The conclusion remains conditional on task 85’s invoked integral presentation and completeness of the \(h_1\)-row set. It concerns only degrees \(d,\ldots,d+b\), not the full quotient or ideal minimality.

## Next
No further conclusion follows without a separate globalization argument.
